title: What Actually Happens When You Tap Your Card?

beats.narration: When you tap your card, your money does not move. Not one single cent.
In the two seconds after the beep, your card turns into a tiny radio.
The chip has no battery. It steals power from the machine, just to whisper.
That whisper is an encrypted code, different every single time you pay.
The terminal asks your bank one question: can this person pay?
And your bank does not open a vault. It just edits a number.
Because your money was never sitting in a box with your name on it.
It is a promise. And when the promise breaks, that is when a bank dies.
